title: Spilling the beans on duplicated genes: unraveling the mechanisms underlying transcriptional divergence in soybean
content: Gene duplication is of great evolutionary importance because it gives rise to new genes (Des Marais and Rausher 2008). By reducing the selective constraints imposed on one or both gene copies, gene duplication enables the acquisition of new functions that contribute toward evolutionary novelty and ultimately adaptation (Arsovski et al. 2015). Duplicated genes arise from either whole-genome duplications that affect all the nuclear-encoded genes or small-scale duplications that are restricted to small genomic regions. Duplicated genes often acquire divergent spatiotemporal expression patterns or variation in transcriptional levels that stem from differences in how cis-regulatory elements are used (Zhang et al. 2025). Key evolutionary insights can be gained from investigating gene expression dynamics and the regulatory processes underlying them in the context of gene pair derivation.
